Q: Cron expression to call bat file with parameter failing A:

Based on the comments from Mofi, and also some thinking about it, I came up with a solution that makes cronical interpret the full path as both arguements and a command.

28 21 * * * cmd /c ""D:\Menelaos\sched_scripts\processReport.bat” server1:5000 dailyOne"

The /C spawns a different process, and the double quotes actually manage to make the system understand that the first part is the bat file, and the other 2 are arguements.

As Mofi also said, the official documentation shows multiple examples with the '/c' argument:

https://github.com/mgefvert/Cronical/blob/master/Cronical/cronical.dat.example

Q: What are the most significant differences between the C language and the Ada language? A:

When comparing programming languages argument to Turing-completeness is irrelevant. That is for "I can program that in machine code." Yes, you can.

C was not designed to deal with hardware. People confuse low-level with hardware, which is not same. K&R used some specifics of the PDP machine they had access to like introducing auto-increment/decrement ++ and --. Alas, it made C less hardware friendly because other machines did not have such instructions. C's hardware unfriendliness caused quite comical situations when char became 32-bit long on some machines. PDP had a flat memory model, so was C, which hit it very hard on machines with a segmented memory - all that stuff with near and far pointers, can you increment at the end of the segment? etc, it was a permanent headache. In Ada you would have no such problem at all, because Ada was actually designed to deal with the hardware.

Q: What alternatives can I use instead of Firebase Storage? A:

This error ("Failed, re-upload later") is pretty common with Firebase Storage in React Native, and honestly, most of the time it’s not Firebase’s fault — it’s usually something small in setup or file handling.

Before switching to another service, I’d suggest checking a few things:

Things that usually fix it

  • Make sure you're converting the file to a blob (React Native doesn’t handle files like web)

  • Check your file URI (file:// vs content://)

  • Add proper contentType

  • Verify your storage rules aren’t blocking the upload

If you still want an alternative

You can look at Supabase Storage. It’s a nice Firebase alternative.

Why people prefer it sometimes:

  • Simpler API (less magic, easier to debug)

  • Clearer error messages

  • Open-source (no vendor lock-in)

  • Storage + DB + Auth in one place
